notes.title: 🔦 Little Lighthouse of Horror – Hotfix v1.0.7.5 is here! 🔦
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224756/e152ad9bc710fa4978bb79d1d7e14e806ad5c983.jpg[/img]
Ahoy, lighthouse keepers! 🕵️‍♂️

We’ve been carefully observing, listening, and reviewing as much feedback as possible, and we’ve packed those improvements into this update. Thank you for your support, reviews, and bug reports, your insights help us make Little Lighthouse of Horror even better!

🛠️ What’s New in v1.0.7.5?
[list]
[*] AutoSave is now enabled by default. No more lost progress!
[*] UI adjustments in the language selection system for a smoother experience.
[*] Added a volume control in the options menu, adjust the eerie atmosphere to your liking.
[*] Fixed a bug in the ending screen.
[*] Various improvements to the game's endings for a more satisfying conclusion.
[*] The crane has been improved, no more unnecessary struggles.
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented interaction after storing food or burning a log.
[*] Fixed a bug that could block the game during the first conversation with Sinclair.
[*] Fixed a bug where the cops could still find the corpse even after throwing it off the cliff.
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed players to kill an NPC without being in front of them.
[*] 🎮 Controller support is here! You can now play with a gamepad.
[/list]

Thank you for playing and supporting Little Lighthouse of Horror! Keep the feedback coming, and we’ll keep improving the game.

See you at the lighthouse… if you dare. 🌊👁️

notes.title: Hotfix v1.0.6
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224756/d465e57a83bd2b21ad34b2b3d94488d443ed98ee.png[/img]

Hello Lighthouse Keepers,

We’re thrilled by the 45+ reviews in just the first week since we launched: thank you for your warm support!
Your feedback helps us keep improving, and today’s update fixes a few more little issues and brings some new improvements:

🔹 Corpse Detection Fix: The body you get rid of will no longer be detected after you’ve disposed of it (take that, investigators!).
🔹 Crane Sound Bug: The crane will no longer keep making noise after reaching the bottom.
🔹 Performance Issues Improved: Optimizations to enhance gameplay performance.
🔹 Shotgun System Improvements: Enhancements for a smoother experience when using the shotgun.
🔹 Expanded Kerosene Can Capacity: You’ll now be able to carry more kerosene for your lantern.
🔹 Crane System Improvements: Further adjustments for better control and functionality of the crane.
🔹 Cutscene Time Bug Fixed: No more time passing during cutscenes (stay immersed in the story!).
Harvest Bark Added: A helpful “E” prompt has been added when the harvest is ready.

We hope you continue to enjoy Little Lighthouse of Horror! For any bug reports, comments, or otherwise, you know where to find us!

notes.title: 🛠️ Small Update - Bug Fixes & Improvements
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45224756/c653e876d00fde223cbcee37b0197b9effd15c50.png[/img]

Hello Lighthouse Keepers,

We're so glad to see many of you already braving our lonely isles, and we've just released a small update to improve the quality of the game.

Fixes & Improvements:
🔹 Dock Barrier Timing: The invisible barrier on the dock now activates a few seconds after the ship leaves, preventing players from getting stuck while collecting goods.
🔹 Language Persistence: Fixed an issue where pressing "Continue" would reset the language to Spanish. Your selected language will now stay as intended.
🔹 Shelf Movement: The shelf can no longer be pushed from the left.
🔹 Dialogue Fix: Mr. Pirie no longer repeats his initial conversation.

We're committed to continuously improving our little horror game, so if you encounter any bugs or issues, please let us know.

Remember: Keep yourself fed, warm, and sane while managing the lighthouse! 🌊🔦

notes.title: Little Lighthouse of Horror is now available on Steam!
notes.content:
In the cold, unforgiving waters off Scotland's Outer Hebrides lie the Flannan Isles, a place where history and mystery intertwine in one of the sea's most enduring enigmas. The disappearance of the three lighthouse keepers in December 1900 has captivated imaginations for decades, spawning theories of madness, ghostly apparitions, and otherworldly vanishings.
It is this story, and its mysteries, that have inspired [b]Little Lighthouse of Horror[/b]: and you can play it today.

[b]About the Flannan Isles Mysteries:[/b]

On December 15, 1900, a relief vessel arrived at the Flannan Isles lighthouse to find it eerily silent. No keepers to greet them, no sign of struggle, just an abandoned lighthouse with meals left uneaten and beds unslept in. 

But what happened? There are many theories. From a freak wave sweeping them away, to supernatural forces being at play. Some even wrote of the madness setting in from the isolation, leading to unthinkable acts. Over a century after the facts, no one knows, and perhaps will never know, what really happened.

Enter "Little Lighthouse of Horror," where you will play as Lawrence, the new keeper stepping onto these haunted isles. The game will take you into a psychological horror experience rich with the same elements of isolation and mystery of the real Isles, with the added difference that maybe you… can survive.

[b]Here’s the main game features:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Sanity System:[/b] Just as the keepers might have succumbed to the mental toll of isolation, players must manage Lawrence's sanity, making choices that could lead to survival or descent into madness.
[*] [b]Resource Management:[/b] The game reflects the keepers' daily struggle with limited supplies, where managing resources like oil and food becomes critical to survival, echoing the real life challenges of lighthouse living.
[*] [b]Immersive Environment:[/b] With its pixel art and atmospheric sound design, the game recreates the haunting ambiance of the Flannan Isles, turning the lighthouse into a beacon of both hope and terror.
[*] [b]Multiple Endings:[/b] Much like the mystery itself, your journey can end in various ways, each influenced by the decisions you make, offering a personal touch to the age old tale of the missing keepers.[/list]
We hope then that Little Lighthouse of Horror not only serves to provide you with a frantic and frightening experience, but also serves as a cultural artifact, rekindling interest in the Flannan Isles mystery (we invite you to do some reading yourself, it’s fascinating!)

Thanks for reading, 

Codiwans (Level Up Gaming Studio)
